What is political economy?

Political economy studies how political institutions, incentives, and economic interests interact. It asks how policies are chosen and how political arrangements influence economic outcomes.

A political economy approach recognises that policies create distributional consequences. Different groups may have different preferences over taxation, regulation, public spending, and institutional change, creating conflicts over policy.
